meta: Estimate your SEPCO bill from units with the 2026 NEPRA slabs, fixed charge, QTA, GST and the latest NEPRA FPA. Upper Sindh summer slab jumps.
author: ali-ahmad

sections.h2: What is the SEPCO per unit rate in 2026?
p: SEPCO is the Sukkur Electric Power Company Limited, one of the ex-WAPDA distribution companies (the youngest company is now HAZECO in Hazara), with its head office in the administration block of the old thermal power station in Sukkur. It bills the same uniform A-1 domestic tariff that NEPRA determined and the Government notified for 2026 for every DISCO. For an unprotected home the rate of the slab the month reaches applies to all units: 400 units are billed at Rs 36.46 each, not slab by slab.

Because the rate steps up with every hundred units, the per unit figure a Sukkur household should look at is the one for its own slab, printed in the table below, not an average. The FPA changes every month and is not part of the uniform tariff; it is pre-filled with the latest NEPRA-verified month, so replace it with your bill's.

sections.h2: Why does a SEPCO bill jump from one slab to the next in summer?
p: Upper Sindh is among the hottest places in the country; Jacobabad and Sibi regularly top the national temperature table, and Sukkur, Larkana and Khairpur are not far behind. A home that ran fans and a fridge on 200 units in March can need an air cooler or AC for most of the day in June, and the units double. Under unprotected billing all of them are charged at the higher slab rate, so the energy charge more than doubles: compare the 400 unit example at Rs 36.46 with the 650 unit example at Rs 41.85.

The fixed charge moves with the slab too, and it is multiplied by the sanctioned kW, so a 3 kW connection pays Rs 2,025 in the top summer month. If the AC is new, check whether the sanctioned load on the bill still fits it with the AC load check.

sections.h2: Which districts does SEPCO serve, and how is it different from HESCO?
p: SEPCO serves upper Sindh: Sukkur, Khairpur, Ghotki, Larkana, Shikarpur, Jacobabad and the districts around them. It was carved out of HESCO, which kept Hyderabad and the southern districts, so an older bill or meter card may still carry the HESCO name. Karachi is served by K-Electric. All three bill the same uniform domestic slabs.

Rural consumers in SEPCO's area often have long gaps between meter readings. A bill that covers more than a month can land in a higher slab than the same use would in a normal month; that is the case the overbilling check is built for.

sections.h2: SEPCO bill check: estimate here, confirm on the printed bill
p: This SEPCO bill calculator estimates the bill from your units and category. It cannot see your account, arrears, the exact FPA for the month or any local charge, so treat the result as a planning estimate and as a check on the slab you were billed in. The printed bill and the payment status are available from SEPCO and through the online bill lookup by reference number.

The full electricity bill calculator for Pakistan explains the slabs and the protected check in more depth; the maths is the same. Every bill also carries an FPA line; see what the FPA line on your bill means. A home on a time-of-use meter can check the peak hours for SEPCO.

faq.q: How do I get a SEPCO bill estimate from my units?
faq.a: Enter the units and sanctioned load from the bill, tick protected only if the bill says so, and replace the pre-filled FPA with the one on your bill under advanced settings. For 400 units on 2 kW the estimate is Rs 20,894, FPA included.

faq.q: What is the SEPCO per unit rate for a home?
faq.a: The uniform NEPRA domestic slab rate for the slab your month reaches: Rs 36.46 per unit for an unprotected home using 400 units. The table above lists the rate for every slab; protected and lifeline consumers pay less.

faq.q: What is the SEPCO tariff for 2026?
faq.a: The uniform A-1 domestic tariff notified as SRO 279(I)/2026: two lifeline slabs up to 100 units, two protected slabs up to 200 units, unprotected slabs of 100 units each up to 700 and an open-ended slab above, each with its own fixed charge per kW. Connections of 5 kW and above are billed on ToU rates.

Not any more. SEPCO was separated from HESCO to serve upper Sindh around Sukkur, Larkana and Khairpur, while HESCO kept Hyderabad and the south. Both bill the same uniform domestic tariff, so the estimate on this page and on the HESCO page is identical for the same units.

faq.q: How do I check my SEPCO bill online?
faq.a: Through SEPCO's own bill lookup, which takes the reference number printed on the bill and shows the current bill, due date and payment status. This calculator estimates the bill from your units; it does not fetch your account.

faq.q: Why is my SEPCO bill higher than the estimate here?
faq.a: The usual reasons are the month's FPA, arrears or a late-payment surcharge, or a bill covering more than a month of readings. Replace the pre-filled FPA with your bill's in the advanced fields; for a long reading period use the overbilling check.

faq.q: Why is my real bill higher than this estimate when it is over Rs 25,000?
faq.a: Usually because of advance income tax, which this estimate leaves out: a domestic consumer not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List pays 7.5% on a monthly bill of Rs 25,000 or more. Who pays the income tax line is explained with the electricity bill calculator.

l.t: Who pays the income tax line

key_facts: SEPCO, the Sukkur Electric Power Company Limited, bills the uniform NEPRA A-1 domestic tariff for 2026 from its head office at the old thermal power station in Sukkur; it has no slab rates of its own.
The SEPCO per unit rate for an unprotected home using 400 units is Rs 36.46 on every unit, giving Rs 14,584 in energy charges before the fixed charge, surcharges and GST.
The fixed charge on a SEPCO bill is Rs per kW of sanctioned load, set by the slab reached: a 2 kW connection using 400 units pays Rs 800, and the per-kW figure rises with every slab.
A SEPCO consumer is protected only while all of the last 6 bills are at or under 200 units on a connection below 5 kW; the first summer month above the limit moves every unit to unprotected rates.

The bill jumps at 700 units: up to there every unit is billed at Rs 41.85, but one unit more moves all of them to the top slab rate of Rs 47.20, which adds Rs 4,480 to the bill of an unprotected 2 kW home.

Income tax is not in this estimate: under section 235 of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001, a home not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List pays advance income tax of 7.5% on a monthly bill of Rs 25,000 or more; consumers on the list pay none.
mistakes: Expecting a separate SEPCO tariff. SEPCO bills the uniform NEPRA domestic slabs; the same units give the same bill as the HESCO bill next door, FPA included, and only the company name differs.
Averaging the rate over the year. The slab rate for a 650 unit June is Rs 41.85; the rate for a 200 unit protected winter month is a fraction of that. Estimate each month on its own units.
Ignoring the sanctioned load. The fixed charge is per kW and rises with the slab, so a 3 kW connection pays Rs 2,025 in a top-slab month.
Paying a bill for a long reading period without checking it. More than a month of units on one bill can land in a higher slab than the use deserves; run it through the overbilling check first.

fields.label: Sanctioned load
fields.hint: The kW printed on the bill; one to three for most homes in Sukkur, Larkana and Khairpur. It sets the fixed charge. A connection of 5 kW or more is billed on peak and off-peak (ToU) rates instead: use the ToU bill calculator.

fields.hint: Tick if every one of your last six SEPCO bills was within the protected unit limit; the bill prints the category.

fields.hint: Only for very small consumers whose bill shows the lifeline category.

fields.name: period
fields.label: Billing quarter for QTA
fields.hint: The quarterly tariff adjustment depends on the quarter the bill falls in.

fields.name: fc_surcharge_per_unit
fields.label: FC surcharge
fields.hint: Financing cost surcharge per unit, from the bill. Secondary-source default.
fields.placeholder: Blank = Rs 3.23 per unit (none on lifeline or protected)

fields.name: fpa_per_unit
fields.label: FPA
fields.hint: Pre-filled with the latest NEPRA-verified fuel adjustment, the one for July 2026 charged on September 2026 bills. October 2026 bills carry Rs 1.11 per unit for August 2026, reported in the news; this page keeps the latest NEPRA-verified rate until that decision is published. Replace it with the FPA rate printed on your bill (negative is a credit). Protected homes pay it too; lifeline bills carry none.

fields.name: fpa_units
fields.label: Units in the FPA month
fields.hint: NEPRA charges the FPA on the units of the month it adjusts (the FPA month, usually two months before this bill), not on this month's units. Copy that month's units from the units history on your bill. Blank = this month's units.

fields.name: gst_pct
fields.label: GST
fields.hint: Sales tax applied to the bill subtotal.

legal.t: This is an estimate, not an official bill. Your DISCO's bill and NEPRA's tariff notifications are the official figures. Do not use this result as evidence before a court, NEPRA, the Wafaqi Mohtasib or any other forum. To dispute a bill, complain to your DISCO first, using the complaint number printed on your bill, then file a NEPRA complaint or a Wafaqi Mohtasib complaint.

content.answer: A SEPCO home in Sukkur or upper Sindh using 400 units a month as an unprotected consumer on a 2 kW connection pays about Rs 20,894: Rs 14,584 energy charge at Rs 36.46 per unit, plus Rs 800 fixed charge, FC surcharge, QTA, the July 2026 FPA and GST. SEPCO bill = units × slab rate + fixed charge + surcharges + GST, with the month's FPA from your bill.

formula.text: Bill = units × slab rate + fixed Rs/kW × sanctioned kW + (FC + QTA + FPA) × units, then + GST
lines: slab rate = rate of the band the month's units reach (unprotected) or slab-wise (protected)
fixed = Rs per kW of the band reached × sanctioned kW
FC, QTA, FPA = per-unit surcharges printed on the bill
